principios.texto: In my deep learning final project I trained four networks from scratch and compared them with paired significance tests. The simplest one won. A bigger model is a hypothesis to test, not a default.

Repetitive work is where automation pays first. At work, that meant the data extraction behind aftersales reporting. On my own time it became stepdub, which records what you do on screen and writes readable Python that does it again.
Since 2013 in aftersales: warranty analysis, fleet maintenance contracts, technical campaigns, and now parts and accessories. The code serves the operation, not the other way round.
